name: sagemaker-mlops
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "1.30.0"

package:
  name: sagemaker-mlops
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/s/sagemaker-mlops/sagemaker_mlops-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: da86b9da3058ce18a66e56755717760c2a4c3d59779bc83ae440f31fe7860901

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: |
    ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
    rm -f $SP_DIR/sagemaker/__init__.py
    rm -rf $SP_DIR/sagemaker/__pycache__

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - setuptools >=64
    - wheel
    - pip
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - sagemaker-core >=2.30.0
    - sagemaker-train >=1.30.0
    - sagemaker-serve >=1.30.0
    - cryptography >=46.0.0
    - boto3 >=1.43.127,<2.0
    - botocore >=1.43.127,<2.0
    - pyiceberg >=0.8.0
    - pyarrow >=14.0.0
    # s3fs is declared by the sagemaker-mlops wheel but is intentionally omitted here.
    # On conda-forge, pyiceberg run-constrains s3fs >=2023.1.0, which pulls aiobotocore;
    # aiobotocore caps botocore <1.43.118, conflicting with the required botocore
    # >=1.43.127 (added in aws/sagemaker-python-sdk PR #6574 for pipeline version
    # aliases). s3fs is unused at runtime in sagemaker-mlops (pyarrow handles pyiceberg
    # S3 I/O), so it is dropped to keep the environment solvable. The pip check in the
    # test below still runs and ignores ONLY the known missing-s3fs line. Remove this
    # workaround once sagemaker-mlops makes s3fs optional (targeted 3.31.0).
  # protobuf arrives transitively via sagemaker-train/sagemaker-serve -> mlflow ->
  # databricks-sdk, which forbids protobuf 5.26-5.28.* and 5.29.0-4. Without this the
  # solver backtracks to protobuf 5.28.3 and `pip check` fails. Soft-constrain protobuf
  # to the databricks-sdk-compatible window.
  run_constraints:
    - protobuf >=5.29.5,<7

tests:
  - script:
      # sagemaker.mlops's import chain reaches AIRHub (via sagemaker-train), which
      # builds boto3 clients at class-definition (import) time, so a region must be
      # set or the import raises NoRegionError. Upstream fix tracked in
      # aws/sagemaker-python-sdk PR #6401; remove this once a release includes it.
      env:
        AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1
      content:
        - python -c "import sagemaker.mlops"
        # Run pip check but ignore ONLY the known, intentional "requires s3fs, which is
        # not installed" line (see the s3fs note in requirements.run). Any other pip
        # check problem still fails the build.
        - |
          problems="$(pip check 2>&1 || true)"
          printf '%s\n' "$problems"
          unexpected="$(printf '%s\n' "$problems" \
            | grep -v 'requires s3fs, which is not installed' \
            | grep -vi 'No broken requirements found' \
            | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' || true)"
          if [ -n "$unexpected" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: pip check reported problems beyond the known s3fs omission:"
            printf '%s\n' "$unexpected"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pip check OK (s3fs intentionally omitted; tracked to sagemaker-python-sdk 3.31.0)"
    requirements:
      run:
        - pip
about:
  summary: SageMaker MLOps package for workflow orchestration and model building
  homepage: https://github.com/aws/sagemaker-python-sdk
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file: LICENSE
  documentation: https://sagemaker.readthedocs.io/en/stable/
  repository: https://github.com/aws/sagemaker-python-sdk

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - papriwal
    - mollyheamazon
    - mufaddal-rohawala
    - nargokul
    - aviruthen
